description.short_caption: Stained cytospin preparation of cerebrospinal fluid showing yeast forms.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a stained cytospin preparation of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Numerous round to oval yeast forms are visible, some with a clear halo suggestive of a capsule. The background contains inflammatory cells, including neutrophils. The staining technique highlights the yeast morphology and their capsule, consistent with a fungal pathogen.
visible_findings: clear halos around some yeast forms (capsule)

Case_08005/figure3.jpg.source_caption: Gram stain of aerobic blood culture.

description.short_caption: Gram stain showing gram-positive bacilli from an aerobic blood culture.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a Gram stain of an aerobic blood culture. Numerous gram-positive bacilli are visible, appearing as purple rod-shaped organisms scattered throughout the field. The background is relatively clear, with no significant presence of other cell types or debris. The staining technique highlights the morphology of the bacteria, which are consistent with gram-positive organisms.
visible_findings: clear background with no significant debris

Case_08005/figure4.jpg.source_caption: Culture of organism on blood agar plate.

description.short_caption: Bacterial culture on blood agar plate showing growth.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a blood agar plate with bacterial growth. The plate is red, characteristic of blood agar, and demonstrates streaked colonies with visible growth patterns. The streaking technique suggests isolation of bacterial colonies. The growth appears non-hemolytic, as there is no visible clearing or discoloration around the colonies.

description.short_caption: Cytospin preparation of CSF showing numerous neutrophils and intracellular gram-negative diplococci.
description.detailed_description: This image shows a cytospin preparation of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) stained to highlight cellular and microbial elements. Numerous neutrophils are visible, characterized by their multilobed nuclei. Within some neutrophils, intracellular gram-negative diplococci are evident, suggesting a bacterial infection, likely meningitis. The background is relatively clear, with no significant debris or other cell types dominating the field.
